tasks.short: Stock, sort and replenish packaging materials

steps.what: Stock and sort product and replenish packaging supplies for machine operation

tasks.design: Keep physical stocking, sorting and replenishment with the operator. Existing production instructions in {OPS_SYSTEM} may guide the work, but this design introduces no robot, sensor feed or uncounted material runner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Materials must be identified, moved and loaded physically.
tasks.enabler_now: Software can display instructions but does not perform these physical actions.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising wrong materials, safely handling them and replenishing without disrupting operation.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can notice damage or an unexpected material mismatch and stop the task.
tasks.altitude: No change to physical effort or operating authority.

reach.task: Clarify a material mismatch before replenishment

evidence.claim: Displaying instructions does not remove physical sorting, loading and replenishment labour; no saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is physical supply handling, excluding purchasing and separate inventory administration.
Operator identifies and handles materials in s1; no structured par level, consumption feed or automatic stock decision is assumed.
Review native instruction access before any future custom tool.
No new software or process is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Material handling equipment and local safe replenishment procedures
research_questions: Which replenishment delays come from material availability rather than the physical handling itself?

already_counted.description: All physical handling and identification remain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with zero upkeep give zero saving. Both ordinary replenishment and material exceptions retain physical time; no administrative baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count and record finished and rejected packaged items

steps.what: Count finished and rejected packaged items at the agreed boundary
Capture counts with batch, time window and disposition
Total and transcribe count entries into the production record
Check finished and rejected totals and confirm the count record

tasks.design: Configure direct count entry and a draft total in {OPS_SYSTEM}, replacing paper-to-screen transcription when present. Keep actual counting, field capture and reconciliation with the operator; do not assume line counters distinguish finished, rejected and reworked units correctly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts captured at the line are added and retyped into the production record.
tasks.enabler_now: Native numeric entry and grouped totals can eliminate duplicate transcription without a model or new counting hardware.
tasks.still_hard: Defining count boundaries, handling rework and reconciling physically missing or double-counted items.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can investigate the physical line and correct an interpretation that arithmetic cannot resolve.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate recording; physical counting and release responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.role: inspector, tester, sorter, sampler, or weigher
reach.task: Reconcile a rejected-package count with its disposition
reach.learn: Count boundaries, rework treatment and evidence tracing

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs for SPC and alarms; this supports industrial data integration capability, not a verified packaging-count feed or labour saving.
Native numeric forms can total manually captured package counts and avoid their duplicate transcription; the proposed allocation is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is package counting and recording, not inspection decisions, reject removal or inventory movements.

Operator produces counts in s1. In s2 the operator captures batch ID, line, interval start/end, finished count, rejected count, units, disposition or rework flag and correction reason. Full 75 hours in s1/s2 retain physical counting and capture.

S3 sums only compatible batch, interval, unit and disposition entries; duplicates and gaps are flagged, never silently estimated. Unknown entries return to manual counting and entry before confirmation.
Native configuration must be tested before custom code; existing automatic counters and arithmetic earn no saving. No new sensor feed is assumed.
S4 checks batch identity, count boundaries, rework treatment and physical plausibility, not only arithmetic. Its full 10 hours include discrepancy investigation.
Review access and applicable national employee consultation requirements; reporting is not repurposed as individual performance scoring.
unknowns: Current paper transcription and native count-entry capabilities
Agreed treatment of rework and count corrections
research_questions: Can direct entry preserve every count boundary and correction while removing transcription, including at batch changes?

already_counted.description: Physical counting and explicit field capture

incremental.description: Maintain count rules, access and correction handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact count snapshot with batch, line, interval, units, dispositions, totals and correction reasons; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100 and R=60+15+0+10=85 give gross 15, less 2 upkeep yields central net 13. High requires a separate 15-hour transcription step; low assumes only 2 hours removable on a mostly integrated line, consumed by upkeep. Physical counting and capture retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep physical supply handling and counting; remove duplicate package-count transcription where present.
reach: Help inspectors trace count boundaries and rework discrepancies
role.ambitious_version: A packaging operator who can explain the origin of each count without repeated recording or expanded machine authority.

job.title: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
